name: Na Pali Coast Kayak
unique: Seventeen miles of fluted green cliffs dropping into the Pacific, with sea caves, dolphins and a beach landing at Kalalau.
buzz: It is a serious paddle with open ocean crossings; guides are excellent and the scenery is unmatched. Not for beginners.

name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park
unique: An active volcano you can drive around, with steam vents, a lava tube and, when the eruption is on, glowing lava entering the sea.
buzz: Check the eruption status before you go; the crater rim drive is excellent regardless. Bring rain gear.

name: Mauna Kea Stargazing
company: Mauna Kea tour operators / self drive
unique: A 13,796-foot summit above a third of the atmosphere, with observatories, sunset above the clouds and a sky that reveals the Milky Way's dust lanes.
buzz: Altitude sickness is real and tours handle the acclimatization; the summit at sunset is cold and unforgettable. Book a tour with parkas.

name: Manta Ray Night Snorkel
unique: Giant manta rays with 12-foot wingspans loop within inches of your mask at night, feeding on plankton in the beam of a surfboard light.
buzz: People call it the best wildlife encounter in Hawaii; the water is calm and the mantas are habituated. Book a small boat.

name: Haleakala Sunrise
unique: Watch the sun rise above the clouds from a 10,023-foot volcanic summit, then bike or hike down through a crater that looks like the moon.
buzz: The 3am alarm and the cold are real; reservations are required and sell out. The crater hike is better than the sunrise for some.

name: Kalaupapa Mule Ride
unique: Ride a mule down 1,700 feet of sea cliffs on a switchback trail into the isolated peninsula where Hansen's disease patients were exiled for a century.
buzz: The history is devastating and the ride is genuinely thrilling; the settlement tour is led by residents. Book far ahead.

name: Waimea Canyon
unique: The Grand Canyon of the Pacific: a ten mile gorge of red and green, with lookouts, goats on the cliffs and a trail into the kalalau valley.
buzz: The colors are unreal after rain; the drive up is steep and the clouds roll in by noon. Go early.

name: Pearl Harbor
unique: The USS Arizona Memorial floats above the sunken battleship, with oil still seeping from the hull, plus the Missouri and a submarine you can board.
buzz: The Arizona is free but timed and somber; the aviation museum and the Missouri are the add-ons. Book the free tickets early.

name: North Shore Surf
unique: The Seven Mile Miracle: Pipeline, Sunset and Waimea in a row, where the world's best surfers ride waves that can close out the bay.
buzz: Watch from the beach in winter and surf the gentler breaks in summer; respect the locals and the reef.

name: Road to Hana
unique: Six hundred curves and fifty-nine one lane bridges through rainforest, waterfalls and black-sand beaches, with banana bread stands and no hurry.
buzz: Start before 6am, drive one way and swim at the stops; the back road is rough and rental agreements may forbid it.

name: Molokini Snorkel
unique: A partially submerged volcanic crater with 150-foot visibility, a coral reef inside the curve and turtles on the outside.
buzz: Morning trips beat the wind and the crowds; the crater is protected and the fish are tame. Seasickness is possible.

name: Hanauma Bay
unique: A flooded volcanic crater with a coral reef and tame reef fish, a short bus ride from Waikiki, with a marine education center and strict capacity limits.
buzz: Reservations open two days ahead and vanish; go at opening for clear water. The reef is recovering and the rules matter.

name: Iolani Palace
unique: The only royal palace on American soil, with a throne room, a koa wood staircase and the quilt the queen made in prison, restored to the 1890s.
buzz: The audio tour is the way to see it and the basement galleries add the overthrow story; book ahead and wear the booties they give you.

name: Bishop Museum
unique: The state museum of Hawaii with a three story Hawaiian hall of feather cloaks and a sperm whale skeleton, plus a planetarium and a science center.
buzz: The Hawaiian hall is the reason to come and the planetarium is good with children; it is the best single introduction to the islands.

name: Hanalei Bay
unique: A crescent bay backed by mountains and a pier, with a river mouth, a reef and a view of the Na Pali coast from the water.
buzz: The bay is the postcard of Kauai and the winter surf is for experts; parking is tight and the north shore gets rain.

name: Kalaupapa Trail
unique: A 1,700 foot cliff trail with 26 switchbacks down to the leprosy settlement where Father Damien served, now a national historical park.
buzz: The trail is steep and the settlement is still home to patients, so visits are guided and respectful; book through a licensed operator.

name: Akaka Falls
unique: A 442 foot waterfall dropping into a gorge of bamboo and ferns, reached by a loop trail through a rain forest of orchids and ginger.
buzz: The falls are the photograph and the loop is paved with stairs; it rains often and the trail is slippery, which is why it is green.

name: Diamond Head Trail
unique: A trail through a volcanic crater and a World War II bunker to a 761 foot summit over Waikiki and the Pacific, with the crater walls around you.
buzz: The bunker and the view are the payoff and the trail is exposed and crowded; reservations are required and the early slot is cooler.

name: Kalaupapa Overlook
unique: A overlook 1,600 feet above the leprosy settlement peninsula where Father Damien worked, with the sea cliffs and the village below.
buzz: The view is the reason to drive up and the history is the reason to go down; the settlement itself is only accessible by tour, mule or trail.

name: Koko Head Crater Trail
unique: A climb up 1,048 railroad ties on an old military tramway to a crater rim view of Hanauma Bay and the southeast coast.
buzz: The stairs are relentless and the view is the reward; go at sunrise, the trail is exposed and crowded later.

name: Lanikai Pillbox Trail
unique: A short steep climb to two World War II concrete observation posts above Lanikai beach, with a view of the Mokulua islands and the windward coast.
buzz: Sunrise from the pillboxes is the photograph everyone wants and the trail is short but steep and rooty; parking is in a residential neighborhood.

name: Iao Valley
unique: A green valley with the Iao Needle rock spire and a stream, where the 1790 battle that united the islands was fought, with a short loop trail.
buzz: The needle and the stream are the photograph and the trail is short; the parking reservation system catches people out and it rains often.

name: Polynesian Cultural Center
unique: A living museum of six Polynesian cultures with villages, canoe pageants and a evening show, run by students from across the Pacific.
buzz: The evening show is the spectacle and the villages are the learning; it is expensive and the luau package is the full experience.

name: Punaluu Black Sand Beach
unique: A black sand beach of crushed lava where green sea turtles haul out to rest and the palms lean over the water.
buzz: The turtles are the reason to stop and the sand is genuinely black; give the turtles space and do not touch them.

name: Hilo Farmers Market
unique: An open air market with 200 vendors selling rambutan, apple bananas, poke and orchid stems, in a town that gets 130 inches of rain a year.
buzz: Go early for the fruit and the poke; the Wednesday and Saturday markets are the big ones and the prices are the best on the island.

name: Maui Ocean Center
unique: A aquarium with a walk through tunnel under sharks and rays, a living reef and a Hawaiian green sea turtle hospital, on the Maalaea harbor.
buzz: The tunnel and the turtles are the family stops; it is a good rainy day and the combo ticket with the harbor cruise is the value.

name: Kauai Plantation Railway
unique: A narrow gauge train through a working plantation where you feed the pigs and pick fruit, ending at a 1930s plantation house.
buzz: Children love the animals and the ride and the rum tasting at the manor is for the adults; the train is short and the grounds are pretty.

name: Maui Tropical Plantation
unique: A working farm with a tram tour through tropical crops, a duck pond and a restaurant that cooks what grows on the grounds.
buzz: The tram is good with children and the farm-to-table restaurant is the reason adults come back; the zip line is the add on.

name: Dole Plantation Maze
unique: The world's largest hedge maze, plus a train through pineapple fields and a garden of tropical varieties, with pineapple ice cream at the end.
buzz: The maze takes an hour and is genuinely fun for kids; the train is short. Tourist heavy but well run.

name: Kauai Coffee Company
unique: The largest coffee farm in the state, with a self guided walk through the orchard and a tasting room of estate grown coffees.
buzz: The samples are free and the orchard walk explains why Kauai coffee tastes different; it is a quick stop on the south shore drive.
